title: Capture Lists Snapshot Values

docs.title: Automatic Reference Counting — Defining a Capture List

hints: A capture list `[x]` copies the value when the closure is created.
`byRef` captures the variable itself; `bySnapshot` captures a copy. Change `x` after creating both.
`let bySnapshot = { [x] in x }` — after `x += 5`, return `[byRef(), bySnapshot()]`.
jsBridge: Swift closures capture variables **by reference** (like JS). A capture list `[x]` copies the value at creation time, which JS has no syntax for; you'd use an IIFE or `const snapshot = x`.

compass.q: In JS you'd write `const snap = x; () => snap`. What does `[x]` add? (Hint: it also works for `[weak self]`.)
Is `[x]` a copy of a class instance or of the reference? What if `x` is a struct?
`[x]` vs `[weak x]` vs `[unowned x]`: what does each capture?
When would you snapshot state before an async task starts, so a later change doesn't affect the request?
